31429:- **§723.5 ⛔⛔ THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE BITTEN US IN A YEAR, RECORDED BEFORE IT COULD.** The straight skeleton of a long narrow rectangle puts the ridge on the **long axis regardless of history**, so every deep burgage plot would get a ridge running **into** the street instead of a gable facing it — backwards, and plausible enough that nobody notices. **Ridge direction is the frontage signal, and it is fully visible in true plan**, which is simultaneously the strongest argument for staying in plan and the thing a naive skeleton destroys. ⇒ **Derive the ridge from the frontage edge, never from polygon proportions**, and if the partition carries no frontage edge, **say so with the measurement rather than defaulting.** Same class as §710.6 and §719.2: an object anchored to one geometry while the drawing used another.
31430:- **§723.6 THE FIFTEEN-FIELD HANDOFF IS THE REAL DELIVERABLE OF THE RESEARCH, AND IT SHOULD PROBABLY BE BUILT FIRST.** Footprint ring with fixed winding and stable indices · per-edge orientation enum · per-edge street reference · explicit primary frontage index · ridge axis · party-wall adjacency · closed-vocabulary building type · eave and ridge height · covering material with minimum pitch · full plot ring · ground slope · a stable per-building seed from a durable id · importance rank · block id · provenance token. ⭐ **The rule: anything the illustrator would otherwise guess must be recorded by the planner, and every absent value must be an explicit sentinel — never a defaultable zero. Silent fallback is how BOTH reference systems fail.** ⚠ **Retrofitting frontage is a PLANNER change, and planner changes reach back into recorded history** — which is why this precedes the visible work.
31431:- **§723.7 ⭐ THE PRODUCT IDENTITY FINDING.** **No tool found, procedural or otherwise, generates market stalls or carts as real positioned objects.** MFCG places exactly one object in a market ward. And under our own constitution a stall is drawable only when the record holds a market day and a trader — so **our market is full on market day and empty otherwise, and market-place encroachment becomes a visible consequence of recorded history.** Nobody else can do this, because nobody else has the history.

31899:- **§802.2 OWNER REFINEMENT (verbatim intent):** "more success with a chosen method reinforces personality drift which may increase liklihood of it being chosen again down the line with a higher weight, failure isthe opposite effect, all of this being complicated by drift and core personality." **CHAIR RULING — THE TWO-CHANNEL COMPOSITION (R3c), refining R3 rather than discarding it:** every executed method teaches through TWO channels — the **practice mark** (small, method-aligned, outcome-independent: you DID the cruel thing; R3 stands) and the **outcome lesson** (larger, SIGNED by result: success VALIDATES — "this is who I am and it works" — deepening the aligned axis hard; failure CHASTENS — pulling back toward core on that axis). Consequence, ruled a FEATURE: reinforcement GENERALIZES across same-axis methods — success at lying makes manipulation likelier too; habits generalize by character, not by verb. **THE CORE-STRAIN ASYMMETRY (the owner's "complicated by drift and core," emergent from ruled arithmetic, zero new machinery):** core-aligned habits are SELF-SUSTAINING (decay pulls toward core, working with them); contrary-to-nature habits hold a STRAINED position that homeward decay constantly erodes — the gentle man who discovers he is good at threats stays formidable only while he keeps making them, and the moment he stops, he goes home. **STABILITY:** failure's chastening is the negative-feedback BRAKE the §802.1 competence loop lacked — odds are never certain, failures land, weight and drift both fall — so the system self-regulates around a character-odds equilibrium instead of ratcheting. The two arms are therefore: **no dangling number outside the baseline** (a NEW number fails), and **every baselined number still cited** (a cleared entry fails, with "delete its entry"). The set can only fall. A fourth arm walks §0 → the high-water mark and convicts a skipped number **even when nothing cites it yet** — the one arm §920's citation-driven census could not have.
32555:- **§921.4 THE ALIAS TABLE IS MACHINE-CHECKED, BECAUSE THE BRIEF'S OWN RISK ROW WAS RIGHT.** An alias table is a place to hide a real hole by adding a line to a JSON file. Every alias therefore carries a **proof** — a file and a string that must still be present in the live corpus — and the proof is **executed on every run**, not left as a comment: `ALIAS_PROOF_ROTTED` when the string is gone, `ALIAS_PROOF_FILE_MISSING` when the file is, `ALIAS_TARGET_MISSING` when a combined-header alias names a target that is not itself a real opener, and `DEAD_ALIAS` when an aliased number has since gained one. **Silencing a genuine dangling citation costs a code change that reds, never a baseline edit.**
